correctness.rationale: Babson–Kozlov Proposition 4.5 provides exact concentration in degree n-m. Reconstructed product-cell fixed-point traces include the internal orientation sign (-1)^(t-q), yielding net sign (-1)^(q-m), and full Stirling inclusion–exclusion derives the target-color character for all 2<=m<=n, including n=m. The sign-absence argument in function modules and rational invariant transfer prove quotient rational acyclicity. Young’s rule gives the m=3 decomposition. Three standalone finite verifiers independently replayed cell traces, ranks and directly computed homology action. Limits: neither numerical tests nor finite-field ranks certify infinite claims, which instead follow from the explicit general proof and cited theorem.
